title: AWS well-architected framework and design patterns
content: 3 min readOct 2, 2023--Welcome to the second round on exploration of AWS! Previously, we delved into Amazon SQS, Amazon Lambda and Amazon DynamoDB:Amazon SQS, Amazon Lambda and Amazon DynamoDB overview | by Salil Apte | Sep, 2023 | MediumBut how was this architecture designed? What ensures that the architecture is robust and secure for large scale applications across horizontals and verticals? Let’s take a look.What are the six pillars of AWS well-architected framework?Operational Excellence: Optimize operations for efficiency and resilience.Security: Prioritize data and system protection.Reliability: Ensure systems quickly recover from failures.Performance Efficiency: Maximize resource performance and utilization.Cost Optimization: Minimize costs while maximizing value.Sustainability: Continuously assess and adapt your architecture by studying its environmental impact and carbon footprint.Pillars of AWS well-architected frameworkThese pillars support development and run workloads according to expected behaviors. This forms the foundation for design patterns commonly seen on AWS which are as follows:Event driven patternConcept: Event-driven architecture relies on events or triggers to initiate and coordinate the execution of services. Events can be generated by various sources, such as user actions or external systems.Use Case: Ideal for scenarios where services need to respond to real-time changes or updates, such as handling user interactions in web applications or processing data streams.Press enter or click to view image in full sizeOrchestration PatternConcept: Orchestration involves the coordination and sequencing of multiple AWS services to accomplish a specific task or workflow. It acts as a conductor, ensuring all components work together harmoniously.Get Salil Apte’s stories in your inboxJoin Medium for free to get updates from this writer.Remember me for faster sign inUse Case: Well-suited for complex, multi-step processes like order fulfillment, data ETL (Extract, Transform, Load), or microservices coordination.Press enter or click to view image in full sizeFanout PatternConcept: The Fanout pattern distributes an incoming event or message to multiple downstream services in parallel. It allows for efficient, parallel processing of data without causing bottlenecks.Use Case: Valuable when you need to broadcast information or perform parallel processing, such as sending notifications to users across various channels or updating multiple data stores simultaneously.Synchronous/Asynchronous PatternConcept: This pattern addresses how services communicate and handle requests. Synchronous communication involves immediate responses, while asynchronous communication allows services to continue processing without waiting for a response.Use Case: Synchronous communication is suitable for real-time interactions, such as user interfaces. Asynchronous communication is advantageous for background tasks like sending emails or processing large data sets without blocking the main application.Press enter or click to view image in full sizeStay tuned for further insights and updates on AWS!In Plain English 🚀Thank you for being a part of the In Plain English community!
